podcast.title: Formation
podcast.body: Last Exit was formed by Sting and keyboardist Jerry Richardson, both of whom were members of the Newcastle Big Band. They were frustrated by the Big Band's conservative repertoire and sought to play more modern rock-era jazz, drawing inspiration from groups like Weather Report or Return to Forever. "This is Whispering Voices, the first single by Last Exit, a band Sting formed with keyboardist Jerry Richardson from the Newcastle Big Band. Richardson and Sting had been frustrated by the Big Band's conservative repertoire and they wanted to play more modern rock-era jazz like Weather Report or Return to Forever."

podcast.title: London Relocation and Breakup
podcast.body: The band's debut garnered attention in London, but the group ultimately dissolved "not long after relocating from Newcastle to London in early 1977." "Last Exit's debut attracted attention in London but not long after relocating from Newcastle to London in early 1977, the group fell apart."

podcast.title: Sting's Early Songwriting
podcast.body: Soon after its formation, Sting began not only singing but also writing material for Last Exit, including songs that would later be adapted for The Police and his solo career. "Soon enough Sting was not only singing but writing for Last Exit, including songs that were later adapted into police and Sting solo songs."
